title: Empty parameter
explanation: The field holds a parameter with no ontology, accession, name or value. A parameter needs at least a name, so the engine cannot read this field.
fixHere: Use the quick fix to remove the line. If the field is required, validation will then ask for it and you can fill it in.
fixInTool: Leave optional fields out of the file when they have no value, instead of writing [, , , ].

tools.fixInTool: Blank template cells become [, , , ]. Fill the cell in the template, or leave the row out of the sheet.

title: Parameter without a name
explanation: The field holds a parameter that has a value but no name, for example [, , , 25]. A parameter is only readable when it says what the value is, so the name cannot stay empty.
fixHere: Edit the field and enter the name of the parameter in the third position, before the value. Several lines with the same problem usually need the same name.
fixInTool: Write a name for every parameter you export. If a value has no name, write it as a user parameter with a name of your own, for example [, , my parameter, 25].

tools.fixInTool: Free-text values from the template become parameters with an empty name. Give the template column a name so the converter can write it into the parameter.

title: Invalid parameter
explanation: The value of this field is not written as a parameter. A parameter has four parts in square brackets: ontology label, accession, name and value. Only the name is required.
fixHere: Edit the field so that it reads [label, accession, name, value]. Leave out the parts you do not have, but keep the commas, and put quotes around a name that contains a comma.
fixInTool: Write every parameter as [CV label, accession, name, value], with the name always filled in.

tools.fixInTool: Check the template cell this value came from: it must hold a term from the ontology list, not free text with commas.

title: Invalid list of parameters
explanation: The value of this field is not written as a list of parameters. Each parameter has four parts in square brackets, and several parameters are separated by a vertical bar.
fixHere: Edit the field so that every item reads [label, accession, name, value], and separate the items with |.
fixInTool: Write lists of parameters as [CV label, accession, name, value]|[CV label, accession, name, value], with no spaces around the bar that matter and every name filled in.

title: Publication not in the expected form
explanation: A publication must be given as pubmed: followed by the PubMed id, or doi: followed by the DOI itself. A DOI written as a web address, or with the prefix twice, cannot be matched to a publication.
fixHere: Use the quick fix to rewrite the DOI as doi:10.xxxx/yyyy. If it still fails, edit the field by hand; separate several identifiers with |.
fixInTool: Write publications as pubmed:<id> or doi:<doi>, where the DOI starts with 10. and has no web address or second prefix in front of it.

tools.fixInTool: Users paste DOIs as web addresses into the template. Strip https://doi.org/ and a leading doi: from the cell before the converter adds its own doi: prefix.

title: Invalid e-mail address
explanation: An e-mail address must have the form name@server. A value that is only a domain, or has no @, cannot be used to contact the person.
fixHere: Edit the field and enter the complete e-mail address of the contact. This cannot be fixed automatically because only you know the right address.
fixInTool: Export the full e-mail address as name@server. If the tool does not hold it, ask for it instead of writing the domain alone.

tools.fixInTool: The contact e-mail cell of the template reached the file as the domain only. Enter the full address in the template.

title: Line does not start with a line type
explanation: Every line of an mzTab-M file starts with a three-letter line type followed by a tab, for example MTD or SML. This line starts with something else, so the engine stops reading the file here. This often happens when a cell contains a line break and the rest of the cell lands on a line of its own.
fixHere: If the line continues the one above, use the quick fix to join them with a space. Otherwise start the line with its line type and a tab, or delete it.
fixInTool: Remove line breaks and tabs from cell values before writing them, for example by replacing them with a space.

title: Mandatory column missing
explanation: A table header lacks a column that every file must have. The engine reports only the first missing column and stops reading the file, so more columns may be reported after you add this one.
fixHere: Use the quick fix to add the column to the header and to every row; fill the cells afterwards. Validate again to see whether another column is missing.
fixInTool: Always write all mandatory columns of the table, even when every value is null. Column names are case-sensitive and separated by tabs.

title: Metadata line is not split by tabs
explanation: A metadata line must have exactly three parts separated by tabs: MTD, the key and the value. Here the parts are separated by spaces or one is missing, so the engine stops reading the file.
fixHere: Use the quick fix to split the line into key and value at the first run of spaces. If the value itself was empty, enter it or delete the line.
fixInTool: Separate MTD, the key and the value with single tab characters, and never leave the value empty.

title: Metadata key not recognised
explanation: The key of a metadata line is not one the format defines. Keys are either plain names such as title, or have the form element[number]-property, for example sample[1]-description. The engine stops reading the file here.
fixHere: Press Edit this line as text, correct the key and press Save line. Look for a typo, a missing number in square brackets, or a dash that should separate the element from its property.
fixInTool: Write only keys the format defines, in the form element[number]-property, and number the elements from 1 without gaps.

title: Mandatory value is empty
explanation: A field that every file must fill has an empty cell. Table cells may never be empty; a value that is truly absent is written as null where the column allows it.
fixHere: Edit the field and enter the value. Only you know the right value, so there is no automatic fix.
fixInTool: Fill every mandatory field. In tables, write null for an absent value instead of leaving the cell empty.

title: Sections are in the wrong order
explanation: The sections of an mzTab-M file must come in a fixed order and each section may occur once: metadata first, then the small molecule table, then features, then evidence. A line here belongs to a section that was already left, so the engine stops reading.
fixHere: If the line has the wrong prefix or is a stray copy, press Edit this line as text and correct the prefix, or delete the line there. The editor cannot move lines: to put whole sections in the order metadata, small molecule, feature, evidence, export the file again from your tool, or reorder it in a text editor and validate it again.
fixInTool: Write all metadata lines first, then each table section as one block with its header line directly above its rows.

title: Table row without a header line
explanation: A table row appears before the header line that names its columns. Without the header the engine cannot tell what the cells mean, so it stops reading the file.
fixHere: If the row has the wrong prefix, for example SML where SMF was meant, press Edit this line as text and correct it. The editor cannot insert or move a header line: export the file again from your tool, or put the header line above the first row in a text editor and validate it again.
fixInTool: Write the header line of each table section before the first row of that section, and write it only once.

title: Column name used more than once
explanation: A table header names the same column more than once. The engine cannot tell which of these columns holds the value, so the table cannot be read.
fixHere: Open the table in the editor, where the repeated column is marked in the header. Use Resolve duplicate column to keep one of the columns and delete the others, or to merge them into one column.
fixInTool: Make the tool write each column once. If two steps of your workflow add the same column, let only one of them write it, or give the other column a name of its own.

title: Used but not defined in the metadata
explanation: Something the file refers to, such as sample[1] in an assay or an ms_run, has no definition in the metadata. A reference needs its target, otherwise the engine cannot follow it.
fixHere: Use the quick fix to add the missing metadata line, then fill in its value. Alternatively correct the reference if it points to the wrong number.
fixInTool: Write a metadata definition for every element that other lines refer to, using the same number in both places.

tools.fixInTool: An assay refers to sample[1] in its sample_ref, but no sample[1] is written. Define every sample an assay refers to, or let the tool export the sample section.

title: Term not allowed here
explanation: The ontology term in this field is not one the validation profile accepts for it. Examples are a unit used where a tissue is expected, or a method term used as an instrument name. Whether this is a warning or an error depends on whether the rule requires the term.
fixHere: Edit the field and replace the term with one that is allowed here; the message lists the allowed terms. Pick the term yourself: no automatic fix chooses one for you.
fixInTool: Map the values your tool exports to terms from the ontologies the profile allows for this field, and write the term's accession and name.

title: A term does not match its accession
explanation: The ontology check could not be completed for a term. A common reason is that the name given does not match the accession, or that the accession belongs to a different ontology than the label says.
fixHere: Edit the field and make label, accession and name describe the same term. Look the accession up in the ontology to see its real name.
fixInTool: Take the accession and the name from the same ontology entry, and write the label of the ontology the accession belongs to.

title: Ontology declared but never used
explanation: The metadata declares an ontology that no parameter in the file uses. This does no harm, but it suggests that something else is missing or mislabelled.
fixHere: Use the quick fix to remove the unused ontology declaration. If you expected it to be used, look for terms written with a different label.
fixInTool: Declare only the ontologies your parameters actually use, or fill the parameters that should use them.

tools.fixInTool: The converter declares a fixed list of ontologies. Write only those whose terms appear in the sheet.

title: Optional field has no value
explanation: A field that the validation profile looks at is empty. It is optional, so the file stays valid, but a value here makes the file more useful to others.
fixHere: Fill the field if you have the information; otherwise you can leave it as it is.
fixInTool: Export this field when the information exists. Leave it out when it does not.

title: No feature section
explanation: The file has no small molecule feature table. That is fine for a file that only reports summary results, but it means readers cannot see feature-level data.
fixHere: Nothing to do if the file is meant to hold summary results only. Otherwise add a feature table with its header line.
fixInTool: Export the feature table when your tool has feature-level results.

title: No evidence section
explanation: The file has no small molecule evidence table. That is fine for a file that only reports summary results, but it means readers cannot see how the identifications were made.
fixHere: Nothing to do if the file is meant to hold summary results only. Otherwise add an evidence table with its header line.
fixInTool: Export the evidence table when your tool has identification evidence.
